incidents.cause: A loss of control during the initial climb for undetermined reasons, which resulted in an aborted takeoff and runway excursion.
A flameout of both engines due to fuel starvation for reasons that could not be determined due to the airplane’s damage.

The pilot’s loss of airplane control during a descent to a diversion airport with only the left engine operating. Contributing to the accident was a malfunction of the right engine throttle, the cause of which could not be determined.
The pilot’s continuation of the approach with excessive airspeed, which resulted in a hard landing and a loss of directional control.
The pilot not maintaining clearance from the runway sign during taxi for takeoff.  A factor contributing to the accident was an icy taxiway.
A loss of braking due to inadequate servicing of brake fluid by the pilot/mechanic, which resulted in a loss of airplane control on the ground.
Landing gear collapse during the landing roll for undetermined reasons.
The pilot’s inadequate in-flight fuel management, which resulted in fuel starvation and a total loss of engine power.
The pilot's selection of a soft, slushy runway for landing, resulting in a noseover.
The pilot's inadequate compensation for wind conditions during landing.  A gusting crosswind was a contributing factor.

The front seated pilot's inadequate compensation for the right quartering tailwind and failure to maintain directional control.  Also causal was the rear seated pilot's inadequate remedial action and failure to regain directional control.

The loss of engine power due to fuel starvation during climbout for undetermined reasons, because postaccident examination of the fuel system did not reveal any discrepancies that would have precluded normal engine operation. Contributing to the accident was the pilot not visually checking the fuel
The pilot's excessive airspeed during the landing, which resulted in his decision to perform an intentional ground loop to avoid a runway overrun.

The pilot's failure to maintain adequate airspeed while maneuvering, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall and spin. Contributing to the accident was the pilot's improper decision to perform the maneuvers at a low altitude and over water.

The failure of the alternate gear extension system, which prevented the landing gear from being lowered. The flight crew’s misidentification of the intended landing runway. The catastrophic failure and disintegration of the No. 6 engine piston, which resulted in a total loss of engine power.
The pilot's failure to maintain the helicopter's rotor rpm while maneuvering at a low altitude over a fruit orchard.
A total loss of engine power due to fuel starvation, which resulted from an overstress failure of a fitting on the fuel supply line and led to an autorotation and hard landing.
The pilot's focus inside the cockpit during the base turn and final approach, which led to a high sink rate developing and a subsequent hard landing short of the runway.
The student pilot’s improper decision-making, which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel starvation.
The pilot’s improper landing flare and subsequent failure to maintain directional control during the landing.

The pilot’s failure to maintain control of the airplane, which resulted in an exceedance of the airplane’s critical angle of attack, and a subsequent aerodynamic stall.
The pilot's improper decision to attempt an aerobatic maneuver at low altitude, which led to an aerodynamic stall and spin from which the pilot could not recover.
